# falcon-v1.141.0 — the supervised seam, reviewed and fixed

A narrowed release, held for two weeks for one reason: the review of the `falcon-cascade@0.12.0` seam found it **not shippable** (#609). This tag ships that seam after every blocking finding was fixed. Each fix landed with a test that fails without it.

## What this tag actually verifies

These requirements reach `verified` at `falcon-v1.141.0`. They are the only claims this tag carries as verified:

| requirement | what it asserts |
|---|---|
| `SWREQ-FALCON-PREARM-P04` | an **isolated** rotor fault blocks arming, with its own reason |
| `SWREQ-FALCON-SUPV-P02` | a failsafe latch is an in-flight device: it **clears on disarm**, and re-arming is permitted (maintainer decision, #564). **Since #633**, re-arming outside the geofence is refused by a dedicated live row, and a battery failsafe is **terminal until a process restart** |
| `SWREQ-RELAY-VGATE-P06` | the Kani scope check scopes against the right base on every event, and sweeps whenever that base is unusable; verified by a **replay** harness, not by greps. Its verification `FV-RELAY-VGATE-006` now carries the `falcon` tag, so the required gate re-runs it |

The transport binding's proofs and end-to-end test, `FV-FALCON-TRANSPORT-002` and `-004`, are verified (#630). The requirement they serve is not: see "Moved out".

## The review, and what it changed

**How it was reviewed.** `FV-RELAY-REVIEW-140` (the v1.140 diff, de-scoped from that tag) and `FV-RELAY-REVIEW-141` were planned as a maintainer-run multi-agent `/code-review ultra`. That review could not run over Remote Control, so the maintainer chose a **local single-session `/code-review max`** over `falcon-v1.140.0...21c9472` (2026-10-27). **This is not the multi-agent review the plan named.** It returned 17 findings, 8 of them blockers (#609). An 18th was found while fixing the 17th. _[Fill in at tag time: the re-review of the final candidate, its type, and its findings.]_

**Blockers, all fixed:**
- **A reconfigure in flight dropped the supervisor**, so the next tick commanded zero motors in the air, and a terminated vehicle could be re-armed (f1, #611).
- **A freshly built supervisor armed past the breadth rows** (battery, estimator, calibration, MotorsHealthy) (f2, #611).
- **An invalid safety configuration was mapped to permissive values** (f3, #611). Since #627, `vehicle-config` fails closed the same way.
- **The step target no longer drove the Takeoff/Loiter hold.** Takeoff and Loiter now latch the hold point on entry (#616). In Mission the target is a **live follow setpoint** (#632, decision "live setpoint, no RTL"). A Loiter entered while moving **brakes, then latches** (#632; resetting the integral was measured worse) (f4).
- **Failsafe bit 7 reported the legacy pre-arm struct, not the 20-row gate** (f6, #612). The legacy struct is deleted (#627).
- **The transport binding could not fly the `@0.12.0` component** (f9). Binding v2 adds Command, SupervisorConfig and Calibration frames, the ABSENT battery bit and NaN rejection (#614), and its hosts enforce the seq-echo rule (#619).
- **`RELEASE-PLAN.md` disagreed with rivet's scope** (f11, #610).
- **The rotor-out fault detector was never re-armed for a second flight** (f16, #632).
- **Every healthy supervised landing with 40–80 ms rotor lag isolated a rotor**, so the rest of the landing flew the 3-rotor law and re-arm was refused (f17, #633). The detector now ignores a residual all four rotors share.
- **A slow ESC spin-up isolated a healthy rotor on the first takeoff** (f18, #634). The fix has three parts:
  - a 0.3 s spin-up guard;
  - a residual judged against a 50 ms lag model;
  - a stall check that isolates a rotor reading near-zero RPM while commanded, in about 0.1 s.

  On SimBackend, false isolations at spin-up fell from 48/60/76 to 4/8/12 of 192 cells at 250/500/1000 Hz. A rotor dead at spin-up is caught in ~0.1 s, on the ground or in the air.

**Non-blockers fixed:**
- the geofence gets a dedicated live pre-arm row, so the table is now **21 rows** (f5, #633);
- the warm-ups are a fixed time at the real loop rate, and `loop-rate-hz` is **advisory** (f7, #633, decided 2026-10-21 in #587);
- the estimator knows it is on the ground after touchdown: worst grounded tilt error 0.999 → 0.002 rad (f8, #633);
- apt retries leave the stalled mirror, and each attempt is capped at 300 s (f10, #631);
- the battery dropped-sample test now judges the acting term (f13, #631);
- the soak ring check fails closed on NaN, inf, a zero RMS and a malformed tick count (f14, #631);
- the cascade sw-arch describes the partition the code runs (f15, #629; the AADL is the side that is wrong, and its fix is separate).

**Disclosed, not fixed:** f12, below.

## Moved out of this release (maintainer decisions)

- **`SWREQ-FALCON-TRANSPORT-P01` moves to v1.142.** Its own falsification clause still holds: binding v2 has **no State frame**, so a host that speaks only the binding cannot see the mode or why an arm was refused. It moves together with the new `SWREQ-FALCON-TRANSPORT-P02` (the State frame), as one further wire revision announced to integrators before it lands.
- **`SWREQ-FALCON-FAULT-P03` is demoted to `implemented`.** Its only verifier, `FV-FALCON-FAULT-004`, still meets its own "isolates a healthy rotor" clause through one named limit: a **300 ms ESC soft-start** (below).

## What ships as code

- **The published component is a supervised vehicle, not a stabiliser (#571),** at `pulseengine:falcon-cascade@0.12.0`, with a `pilot` interface. `pilot.configure-calibration` carries the full 3×3 magnetometer matrix (#611, #586). `SWREQ-FALCON-SUPERVISOR-P01` is `implemented` and scoped v1.142.
- **The supervisor rules have one copy** (#627). `SupervisorHost` in falcon-core is used by the component, the native mirror, the HITL endpoint and the split. Every export reclaims its arena per call (#615).
- **The cascade can run split** into an estimator and a flight-control component (#617, from #585). It is bit-exact with the fused component over 49,929 ticks at 400 Hz and 108,206 at 1 kHz. **It is not published.**
- **The deployment model is the real chip (#591):** i.MX RT1176, estimator on the M4, cascade on the M7, both at 1 kHz, with WCET **unmeasured** (#157). The architecture layer is derived from it (#602, #261).
- **Smaller:**
  - the legacy `hover` scenario is retired (#595);
  - `falcon-ekf` is no longer published (#590);
  - the gz bridge is on gz-transport/gz-msgs 0.11 in both crates that must match (#621).

## Integrator-visible changes

All of these were announced on jess#167 before this tag, as the seam contract requires:
- **Vehicle config:** an invalid `vehicle-config` is refused.
- **Mission target:** in Mission the step target is a live follow setpoint, and reaching it ends nothing. A non-finite target is rejected. One second with no fresh target takes a HOLD (Loiter) and raises the **new failsafe bit 8, `target-stale`**. Bit 8 is up whenever no fresh target is in force, **in any mode**.
- **Loiter:** a Loiter entered faster than 0.3 m/s brakes before it latches.
- **Pre-arm table:** **21 rows**; the new one is `InsideGeofence`. A vehicle outside its fence cannot arm, including the first arm.
- **Loop rate:** `loop-rate-hz` is advisory.
- **Rotor-out detector:** the spin-up guard is 0.3 s at every rate (it was 0.8 s at 250 Hz and 0.2 s at 1 kHz); the stall check needs `motor-rpm`.
- **Battery:** a battery failsafe is terminal until restart. A "pack replaced" command is planned for v1.142.
- **Binding hosts:** hosts enforce the seq-echo rule. The binding test endpoint sends "no target".

## Verification integrity

- **A merge queue replaces "require up to date"** (#588), and **Kani runs once, in the queue** (#600).
- **The Gazebo install is bounded** (#603, #631).
- **HOLD-001's horizontal bars equal HOLD-P01's figures** (#551).
- **Every GitHub Action is pinned to a commit SHA** (#622), and `sigstore/cosign-installer` moved 3.9.1 → 4.1.2 (#624). **This tag is the first release run on both.**
- **Workflow comments now match branch protection** on which checks are required. Verus, Lean, Rocq, spar and Bazel are not required checks.

## ⚠️ Disclosures

- **Known limits of the rotor-out detector**, all measured on SimBackend only:
  - a **300 ms ESC soft-start** is still falsely isolated;
  - a weak but spinning rotor from an airborne start waits for the 0.3 s guard;
  - the lag (50 ms) and stall thresholds (5 % of full RPM while commanded above 20 %, for 100 ms) are **assumptions pending real ESC data** for the BOM's ESCs. A sensorless ESC that reads zero RPM for more than 100 ms during startup would be falsely isolated.
- **The gz HOLD verdict bounds altitude only by the final sample and a 5 s RMS,** and the required gate flies 25 s, not HOLD-P01's 60 s (#609 f12, #546). Defining the hold window and adding a vertical peak bar is a v1.142 item.
- **The verification gate runs only `falcon`-tagged artifacts** (#601). Untagged artifacts' steps are never executed by any gate.
- **`SWREQ-RELAY-VGATE-P06` has no architecture component, by decision (2026-10-23):** CI tooling is not modelled in the flight AADL (#261).
- **`SWREQ-FALCON-EKF-P04`'s text says "Cortex-M7"; the model puts the estimator on the M4.** Recorded, not fixed.
- **Reproducibility:** this tag does not pin its whole build. Three gaps:
  - the Rust toolchain action is `@stable`, and cargo-component and the sibling `rules_*` checkouts are unpinned;
  - most nested lockfiles are untracked;
  - Bazel's crate dependencies are re-resolved at release.

  Pinning this is in scope for the v1.142 manifest work (`SWREQ-RELAY-MANIFEST-P01`).
- **Still open, still flight-relevant:** the attitude ring (#270). Its verification, `RATE-P05`, is scoped v1.142. Rotor-out recovery on the gz plant (#398) is also open.

## Falsification statement

**This release is wrong if any of these is observed:**
- a reconfigure of a vehicle in flight changes its motor commands to zero;
- a vehicle outside its geofence, or with an isolated rotor fault, reaches `Armed`;
- a healthy supervised landing isolates a rotor;
- a rotor dead at spin-up is not isolated within 0.3 s;
- a host streaming no finite target in Mission does not reach a HOLD within 1.0 s.

Every one of these is shown in simulation and on the host. None has been measured on 6X-RT silicon.
